name: Cassava-leaf soup
summary: Young cassava leaves pounded and simmered with bitter eggplant. Go Vietnam says the soup belongs to Jrai, Ba Na, Xơ Đăng, and Ê Đê cooking, including the former Kon Tum area. The city’s 2023 festival list names lá mì and does not print a recipe.
origin: The Vietnam National Authority of Tourism names lá mì among Kon Tum city’s festival specialties in early 2023. Go Vietnam describes canh lá mì for the former Kon Tum area.
taste: Go Vietnam says the pounded leaves make a thick bowl that starts gently bitter, with chili heat and the richness of pork or dried fish, then turns nutty.
howToEat: Pick the tender tip leaves, strip the long stems, wash them, and pound them in a stone mortar. Squeeze off the extra green liquid. Simmer them with cà đắng. Go Vietnam says cooks add shrimp, stream fish, dried fish, pork belly, chicken giblets, or male papaya flowers. Eat it hot with white rice and grilled dried fish.

The same article says fresh lá mì is cheaper than lá bép because it comes off local cassava fields. It does not print a bowl price in Kon Tum. The shops it names are in Pleiku and Buôn Ma Thuột. A Kon Tum city address is Check on arrival.
where: Former Kon Tum, on Go Vietnam, and on the city’s 2023 festival list as lá mì. A Kon Tum street was not printed. Check on arrival.
